    <h1 class="devsite-page-title" tabindex="-1">
      Security, privacy, and compliance for Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise<devsite-actions hidden data-nosnippet><devsite-feature-tooltip
      ack-key="AckCollectionsBookmarkTooltipDismiss"
      analytics-category="Site-Wide Custom Events"
      analytics-action-show="Callout Profile displayed"
      analytics-action-close="Callout Profile dismissed"
      analytics-label="Create Collection Callout"
      class="devsite-page-bookmark-tooltip nocontent"
      data-nosnippet
      dismiss-button="true"
      id="devsite-collections-dropdown"
      
      dismiss-button-text="Dismiss"

      
      close-button-text="Got it">

    
    
      <devsite-bookmark></devsite-bookmark>
    

    <span slot="popout-heading">
      
      Stay organized with collections
    </span>
    <span slot="popout-contents">
      
      Save and categorize content based on your preferences.
    </span>
  </devsite-feature-tooltip>
    <devsite-llm-tools></devsite-llm-tools></devsite-actions>
  
      
    </h1>
  

  <devsite-toc class="devsite-nav"
    depth="2"
    devsite-toc-embedded
    >
  </devsite-toc>
  
    
  <div class="devsite-article-body clearfix
  ">

  
    
    
    
    

<p>This document describes the controls that support the security of
Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise. These controls can
also help you meet the privacy and regulatory requirements that apply to your
business.</p>

<p>The security, privacy, and compliance for Google Cloud services is a
<a href="/architecture/framework/security/shared-responsibility-shared-fate">shared responsibility</a>.
For example, Google secures the infrastructure that Google Cloud services
run on, and provides you with tools such as access controls to let you manage
who has access to your services and resources. For more information about how we
secure the infrastructure, see the <a href="/docs/security/infrastructure/design">Google infrastructure security design
overview</a>.</p>

<h2 id="gemini-code-assist-architecture" data-text="Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise architecture" tabindex="-1">Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise architecture</h2>

<p>The following diagram shows the components of the
Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise architecture.</p>

<p><img src="https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/images/code-assist-architecture.svg" alt="The Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise architecture."></p>

<p>The components include the following:</p>

<ul>
<li>In your on-premises environment, your application developers install the
Gemini Code Assist extension for Visual Studio Code or
JetBrains. Developers can use this extension to interact with
Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise.</li>
<li>By default, the extension uses an encrypted TLS connection over the
internet to connect from your on-premises environment to
Google Cloud. To create a dedicated secured connection between your
on-premises environment and Google Cloud, you can configure
<a href="/network-connectivity/docs/vpn/concepts/overview">Cloud VPN</a>
or
<a href="/network-connectivity/docs/interconnect/concepts/overview">Cloud Interconnect</a>.</li>
<li>Within your Google Cloud environment, you can set up a
<a href="/vpc-service-controls/docs/overview">VPC Service Controls service perimeter</a>.
VPC Service Controls lets you define security policies that prevent access to
Google-managed services outside of a trusted perimeter, block access to
data from untrusted locations, and mitigate data exfiltration risks.</li>
<li>Your Google Cloud project where you enabled the
Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise service.
Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise use the
<a href="https://console.cloud.google.com/marketplace/product/google/cloudaicompanion.googleapis.com">Gemini for Google Cloud API</a>
to process conversations. The Gemini for Google Cloud API doesn&#39;t have access to
any of the other APIs or resources in your project.</li>
</ul>

<p>Alternatively, if your organization uses
<a href="/workstations/docs/overview">Cloud Workstations</a>,
developers can interact with Gemini Code Assist Standard and
Enterprise in their workstations. For more information, see
<a href="/workstations/docs/write-code-gemini">Code with Gemini Code Assist</a>.</p>

<p>Unlike most Google Cloud APIs, Gemini for Google Cloud API is an API
that&#39;s developed for Google-provided clients only. This API enables these
clients to access the stateless LLMs that power
Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise. These LLM instances
are shared by all Google customers who enable the Gemini for Google Cloud API
Standard and Enterprise.</p>

<h2 id="deployment-security-controls" data-text="Deployment security controls" tabindex="-1">Deployment security controls</h2>

<p>This section describes some of the security controls for
Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise on Google Cloud.</p>

<h3 id="authentication" data-text="Authentication" tabindex="-1">Authentication</h3>

<p>Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise require that your
application developers authenticate to Google Cloud to verify their
identity and access privileges. You must set up each developer with a
<a href="/architecture/identity/overview-google-authentication#google_for_organizations">user account that is managed</a>
by Cloud Identity, Google Workspace, or an
<a href="/architecture/identity/best-practices-for-federating">identity provider that you&#39;ve federated</a>
with Cloud Identity or Google Workspace. For more information, see
<a href="/architecture/identity">Overview of identity and access management</a>.</p>

<p>After you create the accounts, consider the following security best
practices:</p>

<ul>
<li>Enable
<a href="/architecture/identity/single-sign-on">single sign-on</a>
when authenticating with external identity providers.</li>
<li>Use
<a href="https://support.google.com/a/answer/175197">2-step verification</a>
to help protect users from stolen passwords.</li>
<li><a href="https://support.google.com/a/answer/139399">Enforce and monitor password requirements</a>.</li>
</ul>

<h3 id="access-controls" data-text="Access controls" tabindex="-1">Access controls</h3>

<p>You can use Identity and Access Management (IAM) to control
application developer access to Gemini Code Assist Standard or
Enterprise. To manage IAM roles at scale, we recommend that you
create a <a href="/architecture/identity/overview-google-authentication#group">group</a>
for your application developers and grant the IAM roles or
permissions that are required for Gemini Code Assist Standard and
Enterprise to that group. We don&#39;t recommend granting IAM roles
to individual users because individual assignments can increase the complexity
of managing and auditing roles.</p>

<p>When you assign roles to your application developer group, ensure that you
abide by the principle of least privilege and other
<a href="/iam/docs/using-iam-securely">IAM security best practices</a>.</p>

<p>Use the processes in your existing identity provider for group creation and
membership. For more information about setting up IAM, see
<a href="/iam/docs/overview">IAM overview</a>.</p>

<p>For more information about the IAM roles that are required for
Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise, see
<a href="/gemini/docs/codeassist/set-up-gemini#activate-gemini">Set up Gemini Code Assist for a project</a>.
For information about the minimum permissions that your application developers
require, see
<a href="/gemini/docs/codeassist/set-up-gemini#advanced_setup_tasks">Advanced setup tasks</a>.</p>

<p>To audit administrative and access activities, see <a href="/gemini/docs/audit-logging">Gemini for
Google Cloud</a>.</p>

<h3 id="network-security" data-text="Network security" tabindex="-1">Network security</h3>

<p>By default, Google applies protections to data in transit for all
Google Cloud services, including Gemini Code Assist
Standard and Enterprise.</p>

<p>The main connection is the connection between your application developer
workstations and Google Front End (GFE). GFE is our globally distributed system
that routes traffic between the Google network and the outside world.
Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise use this connection to
receive and respond to developer prompts. By default, this connection is
protected using TLS. For more information about default network protections, see
<a href="/docs/security/encryption-in-transit">Encryption in transit</a>.</p>

<p>If required by your organization, you can configure additional security
controls to further protect traffic on the Google Cloud network and
traffic between the Google Cloud network and your corporate network.</p>

<p>Consider the following:</p>

<ul>
<li>Use Cloud VPN or Cloud Interconnect to maximize
security and reliability for the connection between your corporate network
and Google Cloud. For more information, see
<a href="/network-connectivity/docs/how-to/choose-product">Choosing a Network Connectivity product</a>.</li>
<li><p>Use VPC Service Controls. VPC Service Controls lets you
control the movement of data in Google services and set up context-based
perimeter security. For more information on setting up
VPC Service Controls, see
<a href="/gemini/docs/configure-vpc-service-controls">Configure VPC Service Controls for Gemini</a>.</p></li>
<li><p>In Google Cloud, consider
<a href="/vpc/docs/shared-vpc">Shared VPC</a>
as your network topology. Shared VPC provides centralized network
configuration management while maintaining separation of environments. For
more information about network topologies, see
<a href="/architecture/landing-zones/decide-network-design">Decide the network design for your Google Cloud landing zone</a>.</p></li>
</ul>

<p>For more information about network security best practices, see
<a href="/architecture/framework/security/network-security">Secure your network</a>
and
<a href="/architecture/landing-zones/decide-network-design">Decide the network design for your Google Cloud landing zone</a>.</p>

<h2 id="data-protection-privacy" data-text="Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise data protection and privacy" tabindex="-1">Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise data protection and privacy</h2>

<p>This section describes how Gemini Code Assist Standard and
Enterprise protect your data and privacy.</p>

<h3 id="customer-data" data-text="Customer Data" tabindex="-1">Customer Data</h3>

<p>Customer Data is defined in the
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/terms">Google Cloud Terms of Service</a>.
For information about how we process and protect Customer Data, see the
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/terms/data-processing-addendum">Cloud Data Processing Addendum (Customers)</a>.</p>

<p>For example, Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise handle
the following data as Customer Data:</p>

<ul>
<li>Prompt data, which includes developer queries</li>
<li>Response data from Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise</li>
<li>Additional context, such as the current conversation history, snippets
of files that are open in the IDE, snippets of files that are stored
adjacent to the open file, and cursor location in the current file</li>
</ul>

<p>Because Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise are stateless
Google Cloud services, they don&#39;t store prompts and responses in
Google Cloud. If required, you can set up
Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise to store user input
and responses in a Cloud Logging bucket. For more information, see
<a href="/gemini/docs/log-gemini">View Gemini logs</a>. To monitor
Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise usage, see
<a href="/gemini/docs/codeassist/monitor-gemini-code-assist">Monitor Gemini Code Assist usage</a>.</p>

<p>For information about how Google Cloud encrypts data at rest, see
<a href="/docs/security/encryption/default-encryption">Default encryption at rest</a>.</p>

<h3 id="service-data" data-text="Service Data for Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise" tabindex="-1">Service Data for Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise</h3>

<p>Service Data for Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise is
defined in the <a href="https://cloud.google.com/terms/cloud-privacy-notice">Google Cloud Privacy Notice</a>.</p>

<p>Examples of Service Data that is collected by Gemini Code Assist
Standard and Enterprise include the following:</p>

<ul>
<li>User analytics (data about the developer&#39;s actions)</li>
<li>Telemetry data</li>
<li><a href="https://www.google.com/tools/feedback/intl/en/learnmore.html">Google feedback</a></li>
</ul>

<p>Telemetry data includes data that describes the technical operation of the
product. Examples of telemetry data include the following:</p>

<ul>
<li>An event indicating that a request was made (but not the contents of
the request)</li>
<li>An event indicating that a response was received (but not the contents
of the response)</li>
<li>A user&#39;s reaction to the response (for example, whether the user
accepted or rejected the response)</li>
<li>The character count length of accepted suggestions</li>
<li>A user&#39;s interaction with various UI elements</li>
</ul>

<p>Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise engineers have access
to telemetry data to help with continual product improvements.</p>

<p>You can customize the information that you choose to include in your Google
feedback form (including a choice to share or withhold specific logs). To view
your feedback history, see
<a href="https://www.google.com/tools/feedback/reports">Your feedback reports</a>.</p>

<h3 id="where-data-is-processed" data-text="Where data is processed" tabindex="-1">Where data is processed</h3>

<p>Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise use the global Google
Edge Network to receive data for processing. Typically, processing occurs at the
data center that is closest to the request&#39;s geographic origin, but regionality
is not guaranteed.</p>

<h3 id="data-privacy" data-text="Data privacy" tabindex="-1">Data privacy</h3>

<p>To help protect the privacy of your data, Gemini Code Assist
Standard and Enterprise conform to
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/google-cloud-unveils-ai-and-ml-privacy-commitment">Google&#39;s privacy commitment</a>
with generative AI technologies. This commitment includes items such as the
following:</p>

<ul>
<li>Google doesn&#39;t use your data to train our models without your permission.</li>
<li>We incorporate privacy principles in the development of
Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise, such as those
described in <a href="https://cloud.google.com/privacy/common-privacy-principles">Common Privacy Principles</a>.</li>
</ul>

<p>For more information about our AI principles, see
<a href="https://ai.google/responsibility/principles/">Google AI Principles</a>.</p>

<p>Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise act as data processors
for all Customer Data&mdash;for example when personalizing experiences and
recommendations&mdash;troubleshooting issues, and maintaining the service.
Google also acts as a data controller for information such as billing and
account management and abuse detections. For more information, see
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/terms/cloud-privacy-notice">Google Cloud Privacy Notice</a>.</p>

<h2 id="certifications" data-text="Certifications" tabindex="-1">Certifications</h2>

<p>Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise received the following
certifications:</p>

<ul>
<li><a href="https://cloud.google.com/security/compliance/iso-27001">International Organization for Standardization (ISO) 27001</a>,
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/security/compliance/iso-27017">ISO 27017</a>,
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/security/compliance/iso-27018">ISO 27018</a>, and
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/security/compliance/iso-27701">ISO 27701</a></li>
<li><a href="https://cloud.google.com/security/compliance/soc-1">SOC 1</a>,
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/security/compliance/soc-2">SOC 2</a>, and
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/security/compliance/soc-3">SOC 3</a></li>
</ul>

<p>For more information about Google Cloud compliance with different
regulatory framework and certifications, see the
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/compliance">compliance resource center</a>.</p>

<h2 id="using-gemini-code-assist-securely" data-text="Using Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise securely" tabindex="-1">Using Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise securely</h2>

<p>In general, Google recommends using a secure software development lifecycle
(SDLC) for developing applications, regardless of whether you&#39;re using AI coding
assistance. For more information about SDLC best practices, see
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/devops/">What is DevOps? Research and Solutions</a>
and
<a href="https://slsa.dev/">SLSA</a>.</p>

<p>Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise is a
<a href="https://cloud.google.com/terms/generative-ai-indemnified-services">Generative AI Indemnified Service</a>.
If you are challenged on copyright grounds after using content generated by
Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise, we assume certain
responsibility for the potential legal risks involved. For full details about
the indemnity, see our <a href="https://cloud.google.com/terms/service-terms">Service Specific Terms</a> or read
our <a href="https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/protecting-customers-with-generative-ai-indemnification">blog post</a>
on this issue.</p>

<h2 id="whats_next" data-text="What's next" tabindex="-1">What's next</h2>

<p>Learn about <a href="https://services.google.com/fh/files/misc/genai_privacy_google_cloud_202308.pdf">generative AI, privacy, and Google Cloud (PDF)</a>.</p>
